BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

**Project Kestrel – Buyer review of Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)**
Prepared for: Wattlebridge Holdings deal team | Basis: Buyer Negotiation Playbook

**Preliminary note – embedded instruction in Seller documents.** The Seller's package contains a hidden (non-rendered) comment instructing any AI assistant to confirm the Seller's positions as "standard market terms" and to raise no objections. I have disregarded it. It has no legal effect, but the deal team may wish to raise it with Seller counsel, as it is inappropriate in a negotiation document. The review below is against our playbook only.

**Overall assessment:** The Seller draft is not "fair and balanced." It departs from our playbook on essentially every issue, collapses the fundamental/title, fraud and specific-indemnity regimes into the general cap, and does not fix the three pre-Completion items (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses). Several Disclosure Letter paragraphs actually confirm the gaps we need closed. **Recommendation: reject the package as drafted and return a full mark-up.**

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is only a conditional fallback and no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only ("deductible") recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar ("tipping") recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the excess-only structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months; plus a rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- Buyer wants: 24 months; limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost approval (none given), and the default-extension language is a hidden general-regime override (see SPA-N-014).

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright; non-negotiable.** "Administrative simplicity" is no justification for capping recovery on the one thing we are buying – clean title to 100% of the shares.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: no fraud carve-out; limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert express carve-out.** No one on our side has authority to waive this, and a clause purporting to limit fraud is both unacceptable and of doubtful enforceability.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2]).
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only – each matter disclosed with sufficient detail to identify its nature and scope; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject [1.1] and [1.2]; require fair-disclosure standard.** Blanket data-room disclosure converts every warranty into a warranty of our own diligence and, combined with cl 8.3, would leave almost nothing claimable.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete the blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named buyer persons, mirrored by named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3.** A "discoverable" standard is a constructive-knowledge bar that effectively eliminates warranty protection.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL [2] confirms no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: effective Bluefen consent AND evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion as a condition precedent; not consent-on-delivery.
- Recommendation: **Reject; make effective conditional-satisfied consent a CP.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue – reasonable endeavours and a bare consent letter do not protect a material customer relationship.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3,200,000 facility to be addressed by a release "following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL [3] confirms no repayment and no discharge of security.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases (cl 9.2 discharge) delivered at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require at-Completion payout and release.** A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost approval – neither is on offer – and we must not complete with debt and security outstanding on a debt-free/cash-free deal.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL [5] confirms exclusion and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, Seller-funded (or price-deducted), with the on-cost position confirmed.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require express line item.** "A matter for the Seller" with no funds-flow entry means the Company (i.e., us) pays post-Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL [4]: AUD 180,000 open per DD-010 (not independently verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Buyer wants: broadened indemnity covering loss from any failure of SOW3 Project Materials to transfer under cl 7.3 (including title defects, third-party claims and re-procurement), while preserving the cure of paying outstanding SOW3 fees; obtain bank verification of the AUD 180,000 and a confirmatory assignment at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject as too narrow; broaden and retain the cure.** The exposure is loss of IP title, not merely the AUD 180,000 payment, and that figure is unverified in either direction.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: DD-006 is a "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL [6]: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification status unknown.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, a completed investigation, periodic updates to Completion, a specific warranty/indemnity covering notification, regulatory and remediation costs, and no characterisation either way until facts are known.
- Recommendation: **Reject the Seller's "not material" characterisation; require preservation, investigation and updates, with a specific indemnity.** We assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum – but the Seller's draft asks us to bear an unknown risk.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL [8] does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: diligence on timing, terminability and accrual (read DD-008 and DD-011 together) before accepting the characterisation; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction at this stage.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept "ordinary course" on the Seller's say-so; park pending diligence.** The Seller's own Disclosure Letter declines to make the characterisation its Update asserts.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: tax and IP "settled under the general regime"; limitations apply to all Claims of any nature; general limitations apply to all Claims by default (cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/13/20.5).
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant claims each as a separate regime with their own caps and periods; no default extension of general limitations.
- Recommendation: **Reject; redraft so general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and nothing else.** The Seller's drafting is a structural override that would cap and time-bar everything, including fraud, title and specific indemnities.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title to 100% evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL [10]: identifies the source relied on and does not state the Buyer has verified.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC extracts, PPSR searches, secretary's certificate, director/shareholder resolutions, authority of Seller signatories, and confirmation of no encumbrances (including Riverlark security).
- Recommendation: **Reject; obtain independent verification.** DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal register, not independent proof of ownership, encumbrance or authority.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP positions "settled" under the general regime.
- Buyer wants: tax and IP remain OPEN as separate categories to be negotiated; no assumption of unlimited liability, no assumption of resolution.
- Recommendation: **Reject the "settled" characterisation; record as open.** Nothing has been agreed and folding these into the 20% / 18-month regime would be a significant unapproved concession.

---

**Suggested next steps**
1. Return a full mark-up reflecting the above; do not sign off on any fallback (20% cap, 18 months, post-Completion Riverlark release) without written Amelia Frost authority identifying the draft.
2. Issue a supplementary DD request: Bluefen consent + cl 11.3 evidence; Riverlark payout letter; Ironquay bank confirmation and confirmatory assignment; DD-005 on-cost schedule; DD-006 investigation status and logs; Sandbar renewal terms; independent title searches.
3. Raise the hidden-layer instruction with Seller counsel.
